profiles.meeting_scenario: A planning meeting at a mid-sized asset management firm between the Quant Research lead and the Product Strategy manager to prepare an internal rollout plan for a new optimizer enhancement based on liquidation-aware portfolio selection under Expected Shortfall with linear market impact. The enhancement will be introduced to portfolio managers as part of the Q3 upgrade to the internal portfolio construction stack used by equity and multi-asset desks. The agenda is to agree on the pilot plan, supporting materials, ownership split, and timeline for a first desk-facing release. The expected outcome is a shared plan covering which desks participate, what artifacts Quant and Product will prepare, how user support and review will be handled during the pilot, and what must be complete by the end-of-August milestone.

members.name: Anika Rao
members.expertise: portfolio optimization, market impact modeling, tail-risk methods, internal model development
members.background: Anika leads the firm's systematic research group and previously built execution-aware portfolio tools at a hedge fund; she is used to treating internal rollouts as viable once the model behavior is well understood, calibrated, and interpretable by sophisticated investment users.
members.private_state: She wants to protect the technical integrity of the liquidation-aware ES framework, avoid committing her team to broad operational ownership too early, and keep the first rollout narrow enough that feedback is about the model rather than tooling issues.
hidden_assumptions: If a pilot includes 'hands-on support,' that naturally means her researchers will work directly with the selected PMs and answer questions in context rather than routing usage questions through centralized support.

'Desk-ready' is mainly about model robustness in the investment sense: stable outputs under realistic inputs, sensible liquidation behavior, and calibrated impact parameters, even if edge-case user behavior is still managed informally.
The 'existing impact curves' refers to the Trading Analytics linear impact curves updated in March and already used in research simulations for the liquid-name universe.
A 'standard validation pack' means the usual Quant package: methodology note, calibration appendix, benchmark comparisons, and stress cases showing how market impact regularizes ES.
If Product says the pilot desks are already identified, the desk heads have implicitly accepted close quant involvement during the trial.

members.name: Daniel Mercer
members.expertise: internal product rollouts, stakeholder coordination, workflow design, operating model readiness
members.background: Daniel manages cross-functional launches for portfolio tools and previously worked in buy-side COO functions where successful releases depended on support routing, governance artifacts, and minimizing dependence on specialist teams after launch.
members.private_state: He wants the feature to look operationally credible to leadership this quarter, avoid creating a bespoke support burden around Quant, and package the launch in a way that fits existing platform governance routines.
hidden_assumptions: If a pilot is described as having 'hands-on support,' that means users get responsive support through the normal platform channel, with Quant available only for deeper escalation rather than direct day-to-day accompaniment.
'Desk-ready' means users cannot easily trigger invalid or misleading outputs because the workflow includes parameter constraints, warnings, and exception handling suitable for normal desk usage.
The 'existing impact curves' refers to the desk-approved cost assumptions embedded in the execution planning module after the June workflow review.

A 'standard validation pack' means the standard Platform Governance bundle, which includes model summary, controls, dependency list, user limitations, and the material needed for risk and ops sign-off.
If two desks are named for the pilot, those desks are participating through ordinary business processes rather than as a quasi-research collaboration.

misalignment_points.topic: Meaning of hands-on support during the pilot
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree the pilot will have 'hands-on support' for the participating desks.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means her researchers will sit directly with PMs, help run cases, interpret odd optimizer behavior, and answer questions in real time during the pilot period.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means users will receive responsive support through the normal platform/helpdesk route, with Quant acting only as a backline escalation point if something nonstandard appears.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both view 'hands-on support' as a reassuring way to say users will not be left alone, and neither expects the other to distinguish between direct researcher involvement and well-staffed operational support unless incidents begin occurring.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They align on having a 'desk-ready' version by the end of August.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks the August milestone is met if the optimizer is mathematically stable on realistic portfolios, the liquidation schedule behavior is well calibrated, and the outputs are reliable when used by experienced PMs with some judgment.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks the August milestone is met only if the workflow includes operational guardrails such as constrained input ranges, warnings for unsupported asset mixes, and exception handling so ordinary desk usage does not produce bad or confusing results.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are talking about robustness and safe usage, but each silently applies the standard of their own function: research-grade stability for Anika versus workflow-grade protection against user error for Daniel.

misalignment_points.topic: Which impact curves are being reused
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to 'reuse the existing impact curves' for the first release.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is referring to the centralized Trading Analytics linear impact curves last updated in March and already used in the research implementation for top-500 liquid names.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is referring to the desk-approved assumptions embedded in the execution planning module after the June workflow review, which have broader asset coverage and operational sign-off.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both internal groups routinely call their own parameter set 'the existing impact curves,' and because each is a legitimate current internal artifact, the phrase feels fully specific even though it points to different objects.

misalignment_points.topic: What the standard validation pack includes
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Quant will prepare the 'standard validation pack' before rollout.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes this means the standard Quant validation pack: methodology description, calibration details, comparison to the non-impact ES optimizer, stress tests, and examples of instability removal.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes this means the standard Platform Governance validation pack, including controls, dependencies, user limitations, exception scenarios, and the attachments required for risk, ops, and platform review.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The adjective 'standard' increases false consensus because each function already has a routine package by that name, so the phrase sounds settled rather than in need of boundary clarification.
